Rugged tablet for Fergus

Fergus is job management software for trades. Its website describes quoting, scheduling and crew management, job tracking through a Job Card, invoicing, reporting and certificates, and says support is offered across Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, with a UK version of the site. The field side runs in the Fergus Go app, which the vendor's site says works on Android and iOS.

For the person doing the work, the app is where scheduled jobs, time entries, job notes, photos, forms, certificates and signatures live. That means a device used in lofts, plant rooms, roof spaces and building sites, often in the rain or full sun, and carried in and out of a van all day, which is where a consumer tablet in a slim case tends to give up.

This page sets out what Fergus publishes about the devices and connections it needs, which Tuga rugged devices meet those published requirements, where a Windows tablet fits for the office side, and how a UK trade business can buy a single unit to try before buying for the whole team.

Requirements

What Fergus needs from a device

Each item below comes from Fergus Software's own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Platform: Android 8.0 or later, from Google Play

    The Google Play listing for Fergus Go (package com.fergus.app, developer Fergus Software Ltd., version 3.13.1, updated 1 October 2026 at the time of checking) has a minimum API level of 26, which is Android 8.0, and shows device chips for Phone and Tablet. The Fergus Go overview article links to that listing and lists no system requirements, so the Play listing is the published figure. Source: play.google.com

  • Memory, storage and screen size: not published

    Fergus publishes no RAM, storage, processor or screen-size requirement for mobile devices in the Google Play listing or the Fergus Go overview article we checked. Source: help.fergus.com

  • Offline: previously loaded data, time entries, photos and notes

    The vendor's 2026 release notes say Fergus Go 3.1.2 (February 2026) lets you access previously loaded data when offline. Version 3.12.0 (August 2026) took Offline Mode out of beta for all users, with timer and manual time entries, photos and job notes queued and synced when you reconnect, a banner showing offline status and a sync state on each record (Offline, Syncing or Synced). Data has to have been loaded while online before it can be viewed offline. We found no vendor figure for how much data is kept. Source: help.fergus.com

  • Photos and videos: device camera and album

    In Fergus Go you add photos and videos to a job from the Album or the Camera, and the vendor recommends setting captured photos to save to the camera roll under Settings, Camera Settings. Each item must not exceed 50MB, album or camera roll videos over 30 seconds give an error, and upload limits apply across web and the app. Only photos and videos can be uploaded in the app; other file types are uploaded on desktop. The article says Files and Photos work offline and upload automatically once you are back online. Source: help.fergus.com

  • Signatures: on certificates and sign-offs, captured on the screen

    For sign-off in Fergus Go, the signer taps the signature box and the signature is captured directly on the phone; once signed, a certificate cannot be edited unless the signature is removed. You can also record your own signature under Menu, Settings, Signature Capture, which the vendor says makes it available for completing certificates, a feature of the Certificates add-on. The articles we checked describe this on a phone, and do not state a screen size for signing. We found no article describing a customer signing a quote in the app. Source: help.fergus.com

  • Tap to Pay on Android: NFC and location on, no Android version published

    The vendor's Tap to Pay on Android article says Fergus Pay must be configured on your account, Location Services and NFC must be on, Tap to Pay must be switched on in the Fergus Go app, and the phone must support contactless payments. It publishes no minimum Android version and points to Stripe's list of supported devices. It does not say which countries Tap to Pay is available in, so confirm with Fergus before choosing a device for it. Source: help.fergus.com

  • Windows: no native app documented, no published hardware specification

    The vendor's site describes Fergus Go for Android and iOS and lists no Windows app. It names no supported browsers or minimum computer specification on the pages we checked, though its help articles refer to a desktop platform and web uploads. Source: fergus.com

Worth knowing. Fergus Go's offline mode covers previously loaded data, time entries, photos and job notes, and the vendor's notes say these sync when you reconnect, so fit a data SIM and load the day's jobs before you leave signal. Offline viewing is not described as covering jobs you have never opened, and we found no vendor figure for how much is stored. Tap to Pay on Android needs NFC, Location Services and Fergus Pay, which the A10, A8, A6 and W10 list NFC for, but Fergus publishes no minimum Android version for it and does not say where it is available, so do not buy a device for that feature without confirming with Fergus. We found no documented barcode, QR or NFC scanning in the Fergus Go articles we checked, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine and the W10's optional scanner and UHF RFID reader are not Fergus features. Fergus lists no Windows app, so the Tuga W10 should not be bought as a field device for it. Fergus does not name Tuga devices, and we do not describe any device as certified or tested by Fergus.
Setting up

Getting Fergus running

  1. Create a Fergus account at fergus.com, or ask your account admin to add the technician as a user.
  2. On the Tuga A8, A10 or A6, open Google Play and install Fergus Go (package com.fergus.app, developer Fergus Software Ltd.). Sign in with your Fergus details.
  3. Accept the device prompts for the permissions your team uses, such as the camera for job photos and location if you use Tap to Pay.
  4. In Fergus Go, open Menu, Settings, Camera Settings and check captured photos are set to save to the camera roll, as the vendor recommends.
  5. Fit a data SIM. Offline work is queued and synced later, but loading new jobs needs a connection. Check the sync state shown on each record after working in a weak signal area.
  6. Do the office work, such as quoting and uploading non-photo files, on the desktop version. On a Tuga W10, use Edge or Chrome and check it with your own account first.
  7. For the A8 or A10, fit the vehicle mounting dock and a 12V car charger so the device charges between jobs; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit a tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out on site.

Questions

Fergus on a Tuga device

Fergus Go's Google Play listing sets a minimum of Android 8.0. The Tuga A8 runs Android 12 with Google Play, so it meets that figure, as do the A10 (Android 14) and the A6 (Android 15). Fergus publishes no RAM, storage or screen-size requirement. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Fergus; these are the vendor's published figures set against the device specifications, so try the app on one unit before buying for a team.

Partly, in the Fergus Go app. The vendor's release notes say previously loaded data can be viewed offline, and from version 3.12.0 time entries, photos and job notes are queued and synced when you reconnect. Jobs you have not loaded need a connection. The vendor does not describe the browser version as working offline.

Check with Fergus first. Its Tap to Pay on Android article needs NFC, Location Services and Fergus Pay, and the A8, A10 and A6 list NFC, but the vendor publishes no minimum Android version for it and does not say which countries it covers. Do not buy any device for that feature until Fergus confirms it for your account.

The A8 suits most Fergus users: jobs, photos, forms and sign-off fit its 8 inch 1000 nit screen, the battery is removable, it docks in the van through its VESA mount points, and it costs £379. Choose the A10 at £449 if your team works in the wet or drops kit onto hard ground, because it is IP68 and MIL-STD-810H where the A8 is IP67 with no MIL-STD rating, or if you want the larger 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen for long forms and plans.
